title: Notification Channels
name: Name
passwordKeepHint: Leave empty to keep the stored password
webhookUrlHint: Each delivery POSTs a JSON payload here. Private and loopback addresses are refused by default (SSRF guard); set NOTIFICATION_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1 to allow them
webhookSecretPlaceholder: Optional, lets the peer verify the sender
webhookSecretKeepHint: Leave empty to keep the stored secret
webhookSecretHint: Used per outbound style: Custom → X-Gw-Timestamp plus X-Gw-Signature: sha256=<hmac(timestamp + body)> headers; DingTalk / Feishu → the robot signing key (query string / body fields); Unsigned and WeCom ignore this field (the WeCom credential is the key in the callback URL)
webhookSignStyleHint: Decides how the signature is computed, where it travels, and how we tell that the peer really accepted the message. DingTalk, Feishu and WeCom all answer HTTP 200 even when they reject a message, so with those styles the body's errcode (code for Feishu) is checked as well and a non-zero value is recorded as a failed delivery. Legacy rows with an empty column behave as Custom
webhookPayloadTemplateHint: Leave empty to use this style's built-in default body. Placeholders: {{vars}} (values are already escaped as JSON string content, so write the quotes yourself and leave numeric variables unquoted). A template that renders invalid JSON or uses an unsupported placeholder is rejected before the job is queued; under the Custom style the signature placeholder cannot be used (the signature covers the body, so referencing it is circular)
smsProviderHint: Which provider API and signing algorithm to use: Aliyun (Dysmsapi) or Tencent Cloud (requires app ID and region)
smsAccessSecretPlaceholder: The Secret from the AccessKey created in the provider console
smsAccessSecretKeepHint: Leave empty to keep the stored secret
smsAccessSecretHint: Encrypted at rest and never echoed back; written only on create/update
smsSignNameHint: The provider-approved signature name (company or app name)
smsTemplateCodeHint: A provider-approved verification-code template: Aliyun bodies use ${code}, Tencent Cloud bodies use {1}. SMS has no free-text channel — the system only fills the code into this template
smsAppIdHint: Required for Tencent Cloud (SmsSdkAppId from console → Applications); leave empty for Aliyun
smsRegionHint: Required for Tencent Cloud (e.g. ap-guangzhou); leave empty for Aliyun
invalidPhone: Invalid phone number (CN mobile or E.164 format)
testSendSuccess: Test message sent, please check the inbox
